longformArticle.deck: One verified movement chain from routine guest movement to rooftop recovery became the kernel for a broader modern threshold legend about elevators.
opening: The chain is compact and bounded: a routine hotel visit, a missing-person escalation, elevator-captured movement, rooftop recovery, and later public retelling.
Its legend life began after the case record ended, not before.

storyBody.heading: From Check-In to Vertical Transit
paragraphs: The story starts in ordinary infrastructure: arrival records, room handling, and normal elevator rides in a late-January 2013 hotel context.
Because the opening phase is fully procedural, the case remains bounded as one verifiable chain rather than an anonymous myth.
This baseline is the anchor point from which the later narrative tension develops.

storyBody.heading: Missing Alert and Institutional Response
paragraphs: When contact stopped, family and authorities converted the event into a missing-person case with formal reporting and search activation.
That handoff is the first institutional boundary in the timeline: private absence enters a recordable public process.
The event no longer belongs to rumor because timestamps and official steps are now fixed.

storyBody.heading: Elevator Visual Chain and Threshold Logic
paragraphs: Released camera records documented elevator movement and the final observed transitions before recovery.
The sequence does not close all questions, but it fixes where and when the observed movement became publicly visible.
At this point, the elevator becomes a threshold object in memory: movement between known spaces with a compressed segment of uncertainty.

storyBody.heading: Search Operations and Roof Route Control
paragraphs: The official response expanded into building-level inspections and service-route checks, especially around restricted upper-level access.
Search details reduced the map of possibilities, giving investigators and the public a narrower geography of what could have occurred.
In such events, uncertainty shifts: it moves from motive claims to specific route and access constraints.

storyBody.heading: Rooftop Recovery and Forensic Sequencing
paragraphs: On February 19, 2013, responders found the missing person in the rooftop water system during maintenance-linked work.
From that moment, the chain transitioned from disappearance to recovery and then to case review.
This is where the event stops as an open search and becomes a closed investigative sequence.

storyBody.heading: From Case File to Legend Template
paragraphs: Public retellings reused the bounded sequence as a reusable scene pattern: confined transit, empty-cabin tension, and an unresolved interval.
The resulting lore is not a replacement of facts so much as a transfer from evidence chain into symbolic threshold language.
That is why this record remains useful as a Legend Origins example: the core incident is fixed, while its meaning broadens through repetition.
